quandoUsar: Asking someone which times of the week they are free, to schedule meetings, on-call shifts, or appointments in one-hour blocks.
Setting up windows that repeat every week, such as business hours or the period when notifications may arrive.
When the result needs to be checked at a glance: the summary alongside merges adjacent blocks into per-day ranges and totals the hours.
quandoEvitar: Use `date-picker` or `date-range-picker` when the choice is calendar dates rather than times that repeat every week.
Use `time-picker` when a single time is enough.
Avoid when precision needs to be finer than one hour: each cell is a full one-hour block, with no half hours or quarter hours.

teclado.acao: Move focus around the grid, one cell at a time.
Select or deselect the focused time slot.
Paint: the destination cell takes the state (selected or not) of the cell focus came from.
Move focus to the first or last day, at the same hour.
Moves through the ready-made presets, “Clear”, and the day buttons (which select or clear a whole day), then enters the grid at the current cell.

acessibilidade: The grid uses `role="grid"` with `aria-multiselectable`; each cell is a `gridcell` with `aria-selected` and a name like “Monday, 9 AM to 10 AM”, and only the current cell is in the Tab order (roving tabindex).
The total hours sit in an `aria-live="polite"` region, the ready-made presets expose `aria-pressed`, and each day header is a button with its own name.
The internal texts (help, “Clear”, “Available”, “Unavailable”, cell names, and the AM/PM clock) are hardcoded in English; only `title`, `days`, and the `presets` labels come through props.
movimento: Each selected slot grows from the center of the cell on a no-overshoot spring curve and disappears with a simple fade; in batch changes (preset, whole day) the cells fill in a wave from the origin.
The total hours change by scrolling: the old number moves up and the new one enters from below, on a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion” on, cell and button transitions are turned off and the total changes instantly.
responsivo: Uses a container query: below 46rem of block width the summary drops below the grid, and below 30rem the days show only the initial.
The grid body has `touch-action: none`: on touch, dragging over the slots selects them instead of scrolling the page, so leave free space around it for scrolling.
desempenho: Each time slot is one DOM element (`days` × visible hours, 84 by default), and during a drag the state changes only when the pointer enters another cell, not on every pixel.
notasIA: Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`: the selection is a list of `"dia-hora"` ids, with the day counted from 0 and the hour on a 24-hour clock (`"0-9"` is the first day at 9 AM).
Without `value` or `defaultValue`, the grid starts with the first five columns selected from 9 AM to 5 PM, except noon; pass `defaultValue={[]}` to start empty.
`startHour` and `endHour` define the rows (8 and 20 by default), `days` the columns, and `presets` the shortcuts, each with a `label` and an `includes(day, hour)` function.

quandoUsar: A blog or news index for a site, with a featured post, category filter, and pagination, all from an in-memory list of posts.
Prototypes and static sites without a router: without `getHref`, clicking opens the post in an in-place reader and “All posts” returns to the index.
Editorial lists with a cover image, summary, author, and reading time on each card.
quandoEvitar: Use `changelog-feed` for release notes, with change type, version number, and month navigation.
Use `infinite-masonry` when the content is an image feed of varying heights that loads on scroll.
Avoid when posts arrive paginated from the server: the block sorts, filters, and paginates the whole list passed in `posts` on the client.

teclado.acao: On a card, opens the post in the reader and moves focus to the “All posts” button; with `getHref`, follows the link.
Activate the category filters, the page numbers, and the “Previous”, “Next”, and “All posts” buttons.

acessibilidade: The cards are links (`<a>`), the filters are buttons with `aria-pressed`, and pagination is a `<nav>` with `aria-current="page"` on the current page.
When the reader opens, focus goes to “All posts”; when it closes, focus returns to the originating card, which is scrolled into view; there is no Esc key to close.
Fill in `image.alt` for each post: it is the cover's alternative text on the card and in the reader; the author avatar is decorative (`alt=""`).
movimento: The card cover travels and grows into the reader image (shared element, no-overshoot spring) and makes the trip back on close, while the rest of the index fades out and gradually reappears.
Changing page slides the content in the direction of navigation, the filter and page highlights slide to the new item, and the height follows with a spring, with no pagination jump.
With “reduce motion” on, the cover does not travel, transitions become a fade, the highlights and height change instantly, and scrolling to the top is no longer smooth.
responsivo: Container query on the block itself: three columns, two below 900px, and one below 540px; below 680px the featured post stacks the image above the text.
The filter strip scrolls horizontally without a scrollbar, and below 540px “Previous” and “Next” show only the icon.
desempenho: Covers use a plain `` with `loading="lazy"` (the featured one loads immediately), so serve files that are already resized; a `ResizeObserver` measures the page to animate the height.
notasIA: Import `BlogGrid` by name to pass props (the default export, `BlogGridBlock`, is only the preview); `category` and `page` support controlled use with `onCategoryChange` and `onPageChange`.
With `getHref` the cards become real links and the reader is turned off; without it, fill in `body` for each post (paragraphs as plain text), otherwise the reader shows only the summary.

Pass `categories` with the same categories used in `posts` (the default is the example list; “All” is added by the block) and ISO dates in `date` (`2026-09-18`), which sort the posts and generate the displayed date.

quandoUsar: A floating create button with three to six quick actions, such as new note, task, photo, or audio, in a corner of the screen.
Screens where a fixed toolbar would take space from the content, such as boards, maps, and capture lists on mobile.
quandoEvitar: Use `dropdown-menu` when there are more than six actions or when each one needs always-visible text: here the names appear only on mouse hover or keyboard focus.
Use `expandable-action-bar` for actions on a selection, with labels and a secondary row.
Use `button` when there is only one main action.

teclado.acao: On the floating button, open or close the menu (when opened by keyboard, focus goes to the first action); on an action, run it, close the menu, and return focus to the button.
With the menu open, focus the next action and wrap around at the end; with it closed, `↓` or `↑` on the button opens the menu and focuses the first action.
With the menu open, focus the previous action; disabled actions are skipped.
Focus the first or last action.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the button.
Closes the menu and lets focus follow the normal tab order.

acessibilidade: The button exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls`; the actions sit in a `role="menu"` as `menuitem`, outside the Tab order, with focus moved by the arrow keys.
`label` names the button and the menu for the screen reader, and each action's `label` is its accessible name: write both so they say what the action does.
Esc and choosing an action return focus to the button; clicking outside closes the menu without touching focus.
movimento: The actions leave the center of the button for their places on the arc, one after another, with a slightly elastic spring that overshoots the point a little; on close, they return to the center in reverse order.
The button icon rotates 135° (the plus becomes an x) and a ring expands from it when the menu opens.

With “reduce motion” on, the actions still leave the center, but with a short shift (0.16 s) with no spring or scale; on close they only fade in place, the icon rotates instantly, and the ring does not appear.
responsivo: There is no collision detection: the arc always opens in `direction` and is positioned by transform, so it can go off screen or be clipped by a parent with `overflow: hidden`.
The radius grows on its own to keep 58px between neighboring actions: with many actions on a 90° arc, the menu takes up well over the 96px of `radius`.
notasIA: Import `BloomMenu` by name: the file's default export is the preview (a capture board), not the component.

The component does not pin itself to the screen: position it with a container (for example, `position: fixed` in the corner) and point `direction` toward the inside of the screen, using the diagonals in the corners.
Each action has `id`, `label`, and `icon`; handle the choice in `onAction(id)` or in the action's `onSelect`, and use `open` with `onOpenChange` only if you need to control opening.

quandoUsar: Card game demos and prototypes: deals one to seven cards from the deck to the table and, with five positions, names the poker hand.
Playful sections of a page, such as a draw or a “hand of the day”, where the dealing animation is the content itself.
Reference example of sequential motion: arc trajectory, 3D flip, and shuffling.
quandoEvitar: Use `card-stack` to go through content cards one by one, with throw and undo.
Avoid in games involving money or an auditable outcome: shuffling uses `Math.random` in the browser and the deck lives in the component state.
Avoid when the cards need their own content: the faces only draw value and suit.

teclado.acao: On the deck, deal a card to the next free position; on the buttons, deal the hand (“Deal hand”), shuffle (“Shuffle”), or start over (“Reset”).

acessibilidade: The table is a `role="group"` named by `label`, and the deck is a button whose name says how many cards remain.
The drawn cards are `aria-hidden`; what is on the table is announced by a hidden paragraph with `aria-live="polite"`, which lists the cards and the name of the hand, in English.
movimento: Each card leaves the deck for its position on the arc (it moves sideways first and then down), lifts slightly and flips face up on the way, with 0.13 s between one card and the next.
“Shuffle” gathers the table and makes the top cards fan out to the sides twice; with a full table, the cards return to the deck before the next hand.
With “reduce motion” on, the cards change place instantly, with no trajectory, flip, or wait between steps.
responsivo: The card width is computed in container units to fit the row (up to 5.25rem), and positions are measured by `ResizeObserver`, so the table shrinks without breaking the row.
desempenho: Only the top five cards of the deck are drawn, plus those on the table (at most twelve animated elements); the rest of the deck is just a number.
notasIA: Import `CardDealer` by name; the default export is the preview with five positions.
The deck and the table are internal state, with no props to control the cards: the only output is `onDeal(hand)`, called on click (before the animation ends) with the table's cards in position order.
`positions` accepts 1 to 7; the hand is named only with a full table and at least two positions, and straights and flushes require exactly five cards.

quandoUsar: Three to five short views of the same subject, such as a project's summary, tasks, files, and team, where the stacked-index-card metaphor helps.
Presentation sections where switching tabs should be a visible gesture: the chosen card rises, drops to the front, and the others settle behind.
quandoEvitar: Use `tabs` for ordinary application tabs, with variable-height content or many sections.
Use `card-stack` when the person goes through the cards one by one and dismisses them, instead of choosing by tab.
Avoid with long content: all cards have the same height (`height`) and the body clips whatever exceeds it, with no scrolling.

teclado.acao: Select the previous or next tab and move focus along with it, wrapping at the ends.
Select the first or last tab.
Enters the selected tab (the only one in the Tab order) and then moves on to the controls of the front card, if any; those on the back cards are out of reach.

acessibilidade: Follows the tabs pattern: a `tablist` named by `label` (tied to the tabs by `aria-owns`), each tab with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and one `tabpanel` per card.
The back cards get `inert` and `aria-hidden`, so neither focus nor the screen reader enters the covered content.
movimento: When a tab is chosen, the card is pulled 58px upward in a short movement and then drops to the front with a slightly bouncy spring, while those that were in front of it step back one level, smaller and dimmer.
The content of the card leaving the front stays visible until the new one lands, and a highlight marker grows at the top of the active tab.
With “reduce motion” on, the stack order changes instantly, with no rise, bounce, or transitions.
responsivo: The folder takes `min(30rem, 100%)` and the tabs share the width equally, truncating long labels with ellipses; below 26rem (container query) the tab icons disappear and the text shrinks.
desempenho: All cards stay mounted at all times (the back ones only hidden), so each one's content is rendered even when it is not in front.
notasIA: Import `CardFolder` by name (the default export is the preview) and pass `cards` with `id`, `label`, optional `icon`, and `content`: without `cards`, an example project folder appears.
Control the front card with `value` and `onValueChange`, or set only the initial one with `defaultValue`.
`height` (296 by default) is the height in px of the body of all cards; size it by the tallest content, because the excess is clipped.

quandoUsar: A product's what's-new or release notes page, with each entry tagged New, Improved, or Fixed and details that open in place.
Long histories grouped by month, where the month bar shows which month the scroll is in and jumps to another.
Notes that call for an image with a caption or a code snippet with a copy button, without leaving the list.
quandoEvitar: Use `timeline` for a sequence of events grouped by day, with no type filters or versions.
Use `blog-grid` when the updates are articles with a cover, author, and full reading view.
Avoid when the change types are different: New, Improved, and Fixed are hardcoded, as are the interface texts, in English.

teclado.acao: On a note, open or close the details; on the filters, turn the type on or off; on a month in the bar, scroll the list to it.
With the notes area focused (it joins the Tab order), scroll the list like any scroll area.
In the “Subscribe” email field, submits; an invalid address makes the field shake, shows the error, and keeps focus on it.
In the email field, goes back to the “Subscribe” button and returns focus to it.

acessibilidade: Each note is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, the filters use `aria-pressed`, and a hidden `role="status"` region announces how many notes remain visible after filtering.
The email has a hidden label, `aria-invalid` on error, and a message in a `role="status"`; on confirmation, focus goes to “Undo”, whose name includes the subscribed address.
The current month and the animated counts are `aria-hidden`; for the screen reader, each month is a `section` with its own heading and the month bar is a `nav` with “Jump to …” buttons.
movimento: The details open with the height on a spring and the content rises from a slight blur; when filtering, the remaining notes slide to their new place while those leaving fade out.
The numbers scroll up when they grow and down when they shrink, the month name enters in the scroll direction, and the month bar's pill slides to the current month.
With “reduce motion” on, CSS transitions go to zero, springs and the error shake are turned off, changes become a cut or short fade, and the jump to a month is no longer smooth.
responsivo: The list scrolls inside a fixed height of 560px (520px on screens up to 640px); below 640px the header stacks and the date and version move above each note's title.
Uses window media queries, not container ones: below 480px the year, the month count, and the total of visible notes disappear.
desempenho: Scroll is read at most once per frame (`requestAnimationFrame`) and a `ResizeObserver` redoes the calculation when the list changes height; photos and code enter the DOM only when the note opens.
All notes stay in the DOM, each with a layout animation; for hundreds of versions, trim or paginate the list before passing `entries`.
notasIA: Each entry needs a `month` equal to a `key` from `months` (both from newest to oldest): entries without a matching month do not appear.
“Subscribe” only validates the email and shows the confirmation, with no submit prop; to really subscribe, edit `SubscribeControl` in the installed file.
Depends on `copy-button` (installed along with it) to copy the code snippets; `defaultOpen` takes ids and, without it, the first entry starts open.

quandoUsar: Prototype or demo of an AI chat product: conversation list and replies that “think”, arrive word by word, and can be stopped, copied, or redone.
Usability tests, guided tours, or presentation pages where ready-made replies (`reply`) are enough and there is no server.
Screens that need to go from desktop to mobile: below 760px of width, the conversation list becomes a drawer.
quandoEvitar: Use `chat-thread` for conversation between people, with reactions, read receipts, and attachments.
Use `ai-sidebar` when the assistant sits in a panel beside the page, rather than on its own screen.
Avoid connecting directly to a streaming model: `reply` is synchronous and returns the whole text; for real replies, combine `prompt-input`, `message`, and `message-scroller`, or edit the block.

teclado.acao: In the message box, sends the text; while a reply is arriving, it does nothing (the button beside it becomes the stop button).
Breaks the line; the box grows up to 168px and then scrolls.
At narrow width, closes the conversation drawer and returns focus to the button that opened it.
On the buttons, open a conversation, create another, send a suggestion, or stop, copy, and redo the reply.

acessibilidade: The messages sit in an `ol` list, each turn starts with “You:” or with `assistantName` for the screen reader only, and a `role="status"` region announces when the assistant is replying.
At narrow width, the drawer gets `inert` when closed and the rest of the screen gets it when open; opening moves focus to “New chat” and closing returns it to the conversations button.
The open conversation has `aria-current`, the send button is renamed “Stop the reply” during the reply, and the copy button becomes “Copied”; the fixed texts are in English.
movimento: Messages rise with a soft spring; the reply “thinks” for about a second with a shimmer on the text and then arrives word by word at the speed of `speed`.
The active conversation marker slides between items, the drawer enters from the side with a no-overshoot spring, and the send icon rotates until it becomes the stop icon.
With “reduce motion” on, springs, slides, and press effects are turned off and the reply appears whole after the “thinking” interval, without the word-by-word effect.
responsivo: Below 760px of the block's own width (measured by `ResizeObserver`), the conversation list becomes a drawer over the conversation, with a darkened backdrop and a button in the header.
Takes `100dvh` by default, with a minimum of 30rem; inside a page or a frame, pass `height` so it does not push the rest of the layout.
desempenho: Uses two `ResizeObserver`s (block width and conversation height, to follow the reply to the end) and one timer per reply; all messages of the open conversation stay in the DOM.
notasIA: Import `ChatApp` by name (the default export is the preview); `conversations` only sets the initial state: after that, conversations and messages live inside the block.
Replies are simulated: `reply(prompt, attempt)` returns the text (blank lines separate paragraphs) and `onSend` reports each send; the “Simulated replies” badge in the header is hardcoded.
Depends on `streaming-response` and `loading-states`, installed along with it; pass `user` to change the example person at the bottom of the list and `assistantName` for the labels.

quandoUsar: An app's command palette: search and run actions, go to other pages, or change settings without taking your hands off the keyboard.
Up to a few hundred actions with groups, icons, and visible shortcuts, where search accepts abbreviations (“dup pr” finds “Duplicate project”).
Quick search embedded in a page or panel, since the component is an ordinary panel, not a modal.
quandoEvitar: Use `combobox` when the person chooses a value for a form field, not an action.
Use `search-field` or `expanding-search` to search content with results specific to the page.
Avoid with thousands of items or server-side search: filtering runs on the client on every keystroke over the whole list and all results are rendered.

teclado.acao: Move the highlight between results, in the order they appear, and stop at the first and last.
Move the highlight to the first or last result (in the field, they do not move the text cursor).
Runs the highlighted result (after typing, the first one); the search is cleared and focus stays in the field.
Clears the search; with the field already empty, calls `onClose`.
Anywhere on the page, move focus to the field while the palette is mounted.

acessibilidade: The field is a `combobox` tied to the list (`role="listbox"`) by `aria-controls`, and the active result goes in `aria-activedescendant`: focus never leaves the field.
Groups are `role="group"` with the group name, each result is an `option` with `aria-selected`, and an `aria-live` region announces the total number of results or “No results”.
`label` becomes the field's hidden label; the component does not trap focus or cover the page, so to use it as a modal, put it in a `dialog` that returns focus on close.
movimento: A single highlight slides on a fast spring to the active result, by pointer or arrow keys, and the results frame follows the list height when filtering.
When typing, the rows that leave fade out and the remaining ones slide to their new place; if the new order moves any row more than six positions, the list switches all at once.
With “reduce motion” on, the entrance, highlight, height, and rows change instantly, with no slide or fade.
responsivo: The list has a maximum height of 342px and scrolls inside, bringing the active result into view; in windows up to 480px, the shortcut keys and the “⌘ K” hint disappear.
desempenho: Search scores all items on every keystroke and each result is a button with a layout animation; a `ResizeObserver` measures the list so the frame follows the height.
notasIA: Although it is among the blocks, it installs at `@/components/ryan-ui/command-palette/command-palette`; pass `items` with `id` and `label` and, optionally, `group`, `keywords`, `description`, `icon`, and `shortcut`.

It does not open or close by itself: for a modal, mount it in a `dialog` when the shortcut is pressed, with `autoFocus`, and close it in `onClose`, called by Esc with the field empty and by the “Esc” button.
`shortcut` only draws the keys on the row, without registering a shortcut; the only real shortcut is the global Ctrl+K/⌘+K, which focuses the field and may collide with one of your own.

quandoUsar: A pricing or product page that compares your offering with alternatives, feature by feature, with your column highlighted.
Long tables where the header must stay visible while scrolling and the “Only differences” option streamlines reading.
Comparisons that must work on mobile: below `stackBelow`, only your column and one competitor, chosen by buttons, remain.
quandoEvitar: Use `plan-comparison` to compare your own plans and billing periods.
Use `sortable-data-table` for real tabular data, with sorting and many rows.
Avoid with many columns: all of them share the width, with no horizontal scroll, until the stacked mode kicks in below `stackBelow`.

teclado.acao: On the “Only differences” switch, turns the filtering of identical rows on or off.
On the competitor buttons (stacked mode) and on your column's call-to-action button, trigger the choice.
With `maxHeight`, the table area joins the Tab order and scrolls by keyboard, with the header pinned to the top.

acessibilidade: The grid is an ARIA table (`role="table"`, `row`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `cell`) named by the title, and each mark has hidden text: “Included”, “Partial”, or “Not included”.
“Only differences” is a native checkbox with `role="switch"` inside the label, and an `aria-live` region says whether all rows are visible or only those that differ.
With `maxHeight`, the scroll area becomes a focusable `region` with the title as its name; the fixed texts (the switch, the legend, “Compare … with”) are in English.
movimento: The included marks are drawn as they enter the screen, in a cascade down your column; when filtering, rows close and open their height with a no-overshoot spring.
In stacked mode, the highlight slides to the chosen competitor and the values swap with a slight zoom; the call-to-action button changes width on confirmation with `doneLabel`.
With “reduce motion” on, the marks appear already drawn, rows disappear and return instantly, the button changes width without animating, and swaps become just a fade.
responsivo: Below `stackBelow` (640px by default, measured on the block itself), it shows only your column and the chosen competitor; the columns also narrow through a container query at 820px and 640px.
The header sticks to the top of the page scroll or, with `maxHeight`, to the top of the table itself; `stickyTop` offsets the height of a fixed site header.
notasIA: Import `ComparisonTable` by name (the default export is the preview with limited height) and mark your column with `highlight: true`; without it, the first one counts.
Values per column: `true`, `false`, `"partial"`, a text (limit or price), or `{ value, note }`; “Only differences” compares only `value`, so different notes do not count as a difference.

Without `cta` there is no button: with `href` and no `onClick` it becomes a link, and with `doneLabel` the button confirms in place. In stacked mode, `compareWith` controls the competitor (the default is the first).

quandoUsar: A contact page or section with a validated form (name, email, subject, and message) that turns into a confirmation in the same card, in the `form` variant.
A support center with several channels (chat, email, sales, community), each with its own detail panel, in the `channels` variant.
Companies with offices in different time zones: the `offices` variant shows each one's local time and whether it is open now.
quandoEvitar: Use `feedback-widget` to collect a quick opinion without the person leaving the page.
Use `signup-form` to create an account, with its own password strength and completion state.
Avoid when the form needs other fields: name, email, subject, and message are hardcoded, and only the list of subjects comes through a prop.

teclado.acao: In the subject group, select the previous or next subject, wrapping at the ends.
In the channel list (`channels` variant), select the previous or next channel and switch the panel, wrapping around.
In the channel list, select the first or last channel.
In a single-line field, submits the form; on error, focus goes to the first invalid field.

acessibilidade: The fields come from `input` and `textarea`, with a visible label, `aria-invalid`, and an error tied to the field in `role="alert"`; a submit failure also appears in `role="alert"`.
The subjects are a `radiogroup` with roving focus and the channels a vertical `tablist` tied to the `tabpanel`; during the swap, the outgoing face is `inert`.
On confirmation, focus goes to the “Thanks, …” heading, and “Send another message” clears the form and returns focus to the Name field; the fixed texts are in English.
movimento: The card changes height on a spring when it turns into the confirmation, while the faces swap by sliding slightly and coming out of a slight blur; the confirmation checkmark is drawn.
On subjects and channels, a highlight slides to the chosen option, and the channel panel adjusts its height while the new content enters in the navigation direction.
With “reduce motion” on, the faces only fade, the height changes instantly, the highlights do not slide, and the checkmark appears already drawn.
responsivo: Container query: below 820px the form drops below the text and the channels become a horizontally scrolling row, without the detail row; below 520px the fields stack.
The office cards arrange themselves in automatic columns of at least 240px (`auto-fit`).
desempenho: The `offices` variant updates the local time every 15 seconds; before mounting in the browser it shows “--:--”, so the first render matches the server's.
notasIA: Import `ContactSection` by name (the default export is the preview with a variant selector); `avatar`, `button`, `copy-button`, `input`, `segmented-control`, and `textarea` are installed along with it.

`onSubmit` receives `{ name, email, topic, message }`: return a promise and reject it to keep the form with the failure message; without it, the submit is only simulated (1.1 s) and nothing leaves the page.
The email “hello@example.com” and the reply times of the `form` variant are written in the code; example channels and offices are swapped through `channels` and `offices`.

quandoUsar: The closing of a landing page with a title, text, and two actions, in the `centered` variant, with faces and a short note as social proof.
A call-to-action beside a product demo, in the `split` variant, with a benefits list and a setup card that completes itself on entering the screen (or your own `visual`).
A single-line launch notice, in the `banner` variant, which can be dismissed and closes the space it occupied.
quandoEvitar: Use `announcement-bar` for a strip at the top that alternates messages or runs a countdown.
Use `newsletter-signup` when the action is leaving an email.
Use `hero-section` for the page opening; this section is meant for the middle or end of the page.
acessibilidade: Each variant is a `section` named by the title (`h2` in `centered` and `split`, bold text in `banner`); the dismiss button is called “Dismiss” and appears only with `onDismiss`.
The setup card and the faces are decorative (`aria-hidden`); actions with neither `href` nor `onClick` swap the label in an `aria-live` region when clicked.
movimento: In `split`, the stage rises on entering the screen and the card checks off the steps one by one, every 0.6 s, filling the progress bar up to “Ready”.
In `banner`, dismissing closes the height with a no-overshoot spring and only then calls `onDismiss`; the actions' arrow advances slightly on hover.
With “reduce motion” on, the card already appears complete, the stage does not rise, the banner disappears without gradually closing its height, and CSS transitions are turned off.
responsivo: Container query: below 860px the `split` stacks the text above the stage; below 560px the actions take the full width, one above the other, and the `banner` becomes a block with the actions underneath.
notasIA: Import `CtaSection` by name (the default export is the preview with a variant selector); all texts have example defaults, so always pass `title`, `description`, and `primaryAction`.

Each action is `{ label, href?, onClick?, confirmedLabel? }`: with `href` it becomes a link, with `onClick` it calls the function, and with neither it only toggles the label, which suits previews and not production.
In `banner`, the close button exists only if you pass `onDismiss`; `secondaryAction={null}` hides the second action and `faces={[]}` removes the faces from `centered`.

quandoUsar: Showing an ongoing activity at the top of a mobile interface, or of an app that imitates a phone: call, timer, or music, compact and expandable.
Demos and prototypes where the pill's shape change between states is the highlight.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast` or `toast-progress` to report the progress or result of a task without taking up a fixed place on the screen.
Use `announcement-bar` for a full-width message at the top of the page.
Avoid for other activities: the call, timer, and music views are hardcoded, and the time, the track, and the mute state live inside the component.

teclado.acao: On the compact pill, expand the activity; on the round buttons, accept, decline, mute, pause, restart, or switch tracks.
With the island expanded, collapses it and, if focus was inside it, returns focus to the compact pill.

acessibilidade: The island is a `role="group"` called “Live activity”; when compact, it is a button whose name describes the activity, such as “Jasmine Brooks is calling. Expand” or “Timer, 4:12 left. Expand”.
The icon-only buttons have names (“Accept”, “Decline”, “Mute” with `aria-pressed`), the timer uses `role="timer"`, and the music has a `progressbar` with text such as “0:48 of 3:34”.
There is no collapse button in the expanded view: Esc and clicking outside the island are the only ways back to the compact form.
movimento: The pill changes width, height, and radius on a single spring with a slight bounce, and each view's content enters from a blur and a slightly smaller scale, already at its final size.
The sound bars pulse at different rhythms while there is audio, the phone in the compact form wobbles while the call rings, and the progress bars advance at a steady pace every second.
With “reduce motion” on, the pill changes size instantly, the content only fades, the sound bars stay still at fixed heights, and the phone does not wobble.
responsivo: The expanded pill has a fixed width of 344px, capped at `100vw - 1.5rem`; the content is drawn at that size and does not reflow, so on narrower screens the edges are clipped.
desempenho: Outside the idle state, a single 1-second interval updates the call, timer, or music, even in the compact form; the sound bars and the ring are CSS animations.
notasIA: Import `DynamicIsland` by name (the default export is the preview with a phone and selector); the component does not position itself, so center it at the top from the parent.
Control `activity` and `expanded` with `onActivityChange` and `onExpandedChange`: declining or ending the call and canceling the timer return the island to `"idle"` on their own.
`caller`, `tracks`, and `timerSeconds` replace the example data; the island is nearly black in both themes because it uses the fixed neutral scale, not the theme surfaces.

quandoUsar: A showcase or demo page of illustrated empty states (no results, offline, inbox zero, page not found), where switching tabs transforms the illustration.
A starting point for your own empty states with shapes that morph, adapting texts, actions, and scenes in the code.
quandoEvitar: Use `empty-state` for a real empty state inside a screen, with title, text, and action through props.
Use `not-found` for a complete 404 page, with search and links back.
Avoid when texts and actions must come from props: the block takes none, and the actions only simulate the result on the screen itself.

teclado.acao: Select the previous or next tab, wrapping around, and move focus along with it.
Select the first or last tab.
On the button, run the scene's action: clear filters, try again, check the email, or find the page.

acessibilidade: The scenes follow the tabs pattern (`tablist`, `tab` with `aria-selected`, `tabpanel`) with roving focus, and the illustration is a `role="img"` with its own description for each scene.
The result of each action is announced in a hidden `aria-live="polite"` region, and the button stays in a loading state while the simulated action waits.
movimento: When switching tabs, each of the illustration's ten shapes travels to a new position, size, radius, and color on its own spring, and the lines redraw a moment later.
With a mouse, the illustration layers shift slightly following the pointer; title and text swap rising from a slight blur, and the text height follows with a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the illustration switches by crossfade, with no shape travel, the parallax is turned off, and the texts only fade.
responsivo: The illustration has a fixed aspect ratio and a maximum width of 360px, so switching scenes does not change the layout; in containers up to 420px the tabs get smaller and scroll if space runs out.
desempenho: A single `requestAnimationFrame` loop moves all shapes by writing directly to the SVG attributes, without rendering React on every frame, and sleeps when everything settles.
notasIA: The block has no props: texts and actions are in `COPY`, inside the component, and the scenes in `empty-states-art.ts`; for a configurable empty state, use `empty-state`.
The actions are local and simulated (clear filters, reconnect, check the email, find the page); to connect them to real data, replace the `act()` function in the installed file.
Depends on `button`, installed along with it; the card takes the parent's width, and the content is limited to 480px in the center.

quandoUsar: A floating bulk-action bar over a selection (files, photos, rows), with the three or four main actions always at hand and the rest a tap away.
Mobile screens or narrow panels, where the compact pill fits over the content and opens into a labeled grid only when requested.
quandoEvitar: Use `overflow-actions` for a fixed bar that moves to a “more” menu only the actions that do not fit the width.
Use `bloom-menu` to create new items from a floating button, without a selection.
Use `dropdown-menu` when the action list is long or has submenus.

teclado.acao: Move focus between all the bar's buttons, including the expand button and those of the secondary row, wrapping around.
Focus the first or last button of the bar.
With the bar expanded, collapses it and returns focus to the expand button.
Trigger the focused action, or expand and collapse the bar on the arrow button.

acessibilidade: The bar is a horizontal `role="toolbar"` with the fixed name “Actions”, and the expand button has `aria-expanded` and the name “Show all actions” or “Show fewer actions”.
In the compact form, each button gets `aria-label` and `title` with the action's `label`; when expanded, the visible text becomes the name. The secondary row is a `group` named by `shortcutsLabel`.
All buttons are in the Tab order (there is no roving focus); the arrow keys are an extra shortcut for moving through them.
movimento: The bar is a window that changes width and height on a spring with a slight bounce, growing upward from the pill, while the icons that were already there slide to their new place.
The extra icons appear in a cascade, the labels rise right after, and the arrow rotates 180°; when `label` changes, the new text enters from below and the old one exits above.
With “reduce motion” on, the bar takes the new size instantly and icons and labels just appear, with no slide or cascade.
responsivo: The expanded width is `width` (416px by default), limited to the container's space; the secondary row scrolls horizontally, with a faded end edge indicating there is more.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` follows the container and the content, and only a new target size triggers the spring, so resizing the window does not restart the animation on every frame.
notasIA: Import `ExpandableActionBar` by name (the default export is the preview with the file board) and mark the compact pill's three or four actions with `primary: true`.
The component takes the parent's width and anchors to its bottom edge: position the parent (for example, `position: absolute` at the footer) and show the bar only when there is a selection.
Handle clicks in `onAction(id)` and `onShortcut(id)`; `label` (such as “3 selected”) is the text that swaps with animation, and `shortcuts={[]}` removes the secondary row.

quandoUsar: An app bottom bar or compact switcher with four or five destinations, where only the active one needs to show its name.
Navigation through familiar icons (home, search, inbox, profile), with an unread counter on the icon (`badge: 3`).
quandoEvitar: Use `tabs` or `segmented-control` when all labels must stay visible at all times.
Use `morphing-tabs` when the tabs have labels and the highlight should travel between them.
Avoid with ambiguous icons or many destinations: the names are hidden and the list neither scrolls nor wraps.

teclado.acao: Select the previous or next tab, skipping disabled ones and wrapping around, and move focus along with it.
Select the first or last enabled tab.

acessibilidade: Follows the tabs pattern with roving focus: a `tablist` named by `label`, `aria-selected` on each tab and, when there is `content`, a `tabpanel` tied to the active tab.
Each tab's name is always the `label` (with “, 3 new” when there is a `badge`), even with the text hidden; the visible label is `aria-hidden` so it is not read twice.
movimento: The active tab's label opens on a no-overshoot spring while the previous one's closes, the highlight background grows from the tab itself, and the icon pulses once.
When there is `content`, the panel swaps rising from a slight blur.
With “reduce motion” on, labels and panels swap instantly, with no pulse or blur, and the background's CSS transitions are turned off.
responsivo: The list centers itself and grows with the active label, with no scrolling or line wrapping: check that the icons plus the longest label fit on the narrowest screen.
notasIA: Import `ExpandableTabs` by name (the default export is an app preview); each tab needs `id`, `label`, and `icon`, and counts above 9 in `tab.badge` appear as “9+”.
Without `content` on any tab, it becomes a simple switcher, with no `tabpanel`: use `value` and `onValueChange` to switch the screen externally, as in a bottom bar.
With `content`, the panel appears above the list; to pin the bar to the bottom of the screen, position the component from the parent.

quandoUsar: A frequently-asked-questions section on a product or pricing page, with answers that open in place, in the `accordion` variant.
Many questions grouped by topic, in the `columns` variant, with a category rail that stays fixed beside them while scrolling.
Help centers where the person searches by word: the `search` variant filters questions and answers, ignores accents, and highlights the match.
quandoEvitar: Use `accordion` to reveal sections of any content, not just questions with text answers.
Avoid when answers need links, lists, or formatting: `answer` is plain text, because it is also what the search compares and highlights.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next question in the same list, wrapping around.
Focus the first or last question in the list.
Open or close the answer of the focused question; on the `columns` categories, switch the topic.

acessibilidade: Each question is a button inside an `h3`, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the answer is a `region` named by the question itself.
In search, the count of answers found is announced in an `aria-live` region; on the categories, the active topic uses `aria-pressed`.
`title` becomes the `h2` that names the section; the contact card at the end is a link when it receives `href` and a button otherwise.
movimento: The answer opens with the height on a no-overshoot spring and the text descends from a slight blur, while the plus sign rotates 45° and becomes an x.
In search, questions that stop matching close their height and the remaining ones slide; in `columns`, the new topic's list enters in the direction of the switch and the highlight slides to it.
With “reduce motion” on, answers, filters, and topics swap instantly and the icon does not animate.
responsivo: Container query: below 760px the `columns` rail stops being fixed and the categories become a horizontally scrolling row above the questions.
notasIA: Import `FaqSection` by name (the default export is the preview with a selector) and choose `variant`: `accordion`, `columns`, or `search`; `search-field` and `segmented-control` come along.
By default the first question opens and only one stays open at a time: use `multiple` for several and `defaultValue={[]}` to start closed; each item's id is `id` or, without it, the question.
In `columns`, give each item a `category` (without it, it becomes “General”); `contact={null}` removes the “Still have a question?” card, which does nothing without `href` or `onClick`.

quandoUsar: Collecting quick feedback on any page (help center, article, dashboard) with a fixed button in the corner that does not take the person away from what they were doing.
One-click satisfaction surveys, with five faces and an optional message.
quandoEvitar: Use `contact-section` when the message needs name, email, and subject in order to get a reply.
Use `rating` for a score inside a form.
Avoid with another floating button in the same corner, such as a support chat: the widget is fixed to the bottom corner, on a high layer (`z-index: 50`), and the two would compete for the spot.

teclado.acao: On the “Feedback” button, open the form and move focus to the first face.
In the faces group, choose the previous or next one, wrapping around; with no choice, `→` and `↓` start at the first and `←` and `↑` at the last.
In the message field, submit the form, as long as a face has been chosen.
Closes the form and returns focus to the button, except during submission.

acessibilidade: The button has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; the panel is a `role="dialog"` named by the title, but not modal: focus is not trapped, and Esc or a click outside closes it and returns focus to the button.
The faces form a `radiogroup` with roving focus and names (from “Terrible” to “Great”), and the name of the chosen face is announced in an `aria-live` region.
Submission exposes `aria-busy`, the failure appears in `role="alert"` and the thank-you in `role="status"`; the message field has the hidden label “Your feedback”.
movimento: The button itself transforms into the panel, from its corner, on a no-overshoot layout spring, and the content appears gradually right after.
The highlight slides to the chosen face, which grows and rotates slightly; on completion, the badge appears with a bounce, the checkmark is drawn, and the panel closes by itself after 2.6 s.
With “reduce motion” on, the panel opens and closes instantly, with no morph or rotation, and the submit indicator stays still.
responsivo: It stays fixed to the window (`position: fixed`) in the corner chosen by `placement`; with `contained`, it attaches to the nearest positioned ancestor, as in a panel or a preview.
The panel is 21rem wide, limited to the available space; on screens up to 30rem, the distance to the edges shrinks.
notasIA: Import `FeedbackWidget` by name (the default export is the preview with a help article) and mount it once in the page layout: it pins itself to the corner.
`onSubmit` receives `{ mood, message }`, with the message already trimmed: return a promise to hold the submitting state and reject it to show the error and keep the form.
The face names and the failure, submitting, and “Close” texts are hardcoded in English; `label`, `title`, `placeholder`, `thanksTitle`, and `thanksMessage` come through props.

quandoUsar: Forms that ask for one or more files with type and size rules, showing the reason for rejection on the file's own row.
Upload with per-file progress, cancellation on removal, and a retry button on failure, wired to your `onUpload`.
quandoEvitar: Use `file-dropzone` when a generous area to drop files is enough, with no list or progress.
Avoid for choosing a profile image with cropping or a preview: each row shows only a type icon, the name, and the size.

teclado.acao: On the upload area, open the system file-picker window.
On each row's buttons, remove the file or retry; on removal, focus goes to the neighboring file's “remove” or back to the upload area.

acessibilidade: The upload area is a focusable `role="button"`, with `aria-disabled` and the description tied by `aria-describedby`; the real file `input` is hidden and out of the Tab order.
An `aria-live` region announces files added, rejected, uploaded, failed, and removed, and each row's buttons include the file name (“Remove foto.png”, “Retry foto.png”).
movimento: Each row opens and closes its height on a spring; the progress bar and the percentage follow the same spring, and the bar only collapses after showing 100%.
The status texts swap rising from a slight blur, the done checkmark is drawn, and the cloud rises slightly when a file hovers over the area.
With “reduce motion” on, rows, bar, and texts change instantly or only fade, and the cloud does not move.
desempenho: Each upload has its own `AbortController`: removing the file or unmounting the component cancels the signal, so your `onUpload` must respect `signal` to stop the network request.
notasIA: Although it is among the blocks, it installs at `@/components/ryan-ui/file-upload/file-upload`; without `onUpload`, files just appear as ready and nothing is sent.

`onUpload(file, { onProgress, signal })` must call `onProgress` from 0 to 100, resolve when finished, and reject on failure; files rejected by `accept` or `maxSize` (in bytes) stay in the list and are not sent.
`value` and `onChange` control the `{ id, file, error }` list; with `multiple={false}`, a new file replaces the previous one and cancels the upload in progress.

quandoUsar: The opening of a product landing page: a live product window (`product`), an automation flow running (`workflow`), or large typography over a word strip (`editorial`).
A hero with your own content (title, description, actions, install command, and a visual beside it), passing `title`, without building the layout from scratch.
quandoEvitar: Use `cta-section` for a call to action in the middle or end of the page.
Use `site-header` for site navigation: the bar in the built-in versions scrolls along with the hero and loses its links on narrow screens.
Avoid using the built-in versions with your brand without editing the code: texts, numbers, and names (Lumen, Relay, Cadence) are examples, and only the actions come through props.
acessibilidade: Each version has a single `h1`; the floating cards are `aria-hidden`, and the product window and the graph are groups with a summary name, such as “Lumen revenue dashboard, sample data”.
In the graph, each step has a named state (“Running”, “Done”, “Skipped”, “Waiting”), and the phrase under the highlighter is drawn twice, with the copy in `aria-hidden`, so it is read only once.
movimento: On mount, the parts rise in reading order coming out of a slight blur, and a highlighter in the accent color sweeps left to right over a phrase of the title.
In `product`, the numbers scroll, the chart is drawn, and the cards float; in `workflow`, a pulse travels along the lines on each event; in `editorial`, the words run along a strip.

With “reduce motion” on, nothing moves (it only fades), the chart already appears ready, the flow shows each event as completed, the strip becomes an ordinary scroll area, and the highlighter comes already painted.
responsivo: The built-in versions take at least the screen height (`100svh`) and adjust through a container query; below 760px the bar links and “Sign in” disappear, with no menu in their place.
In `workflow`, the graph is drawn at a fixed size and scaled down to fit the column, with a narrow arrangement below 520px.
desempenho: The event and notice loops stop when the hero leaves the screen or the tab is hidden (`IntersectionObserver` and `visibilitychange`); even so, use one version per page.
notasIA: Import `HeroSection` by name (the default export is the preview with a version selector) and choose `variant`: `product`, `workflow`, or `editorial`; `centered`, `split`, and `minimal` also work.

With `title`, the block replaces the showcase with your content (`description`, `announcement`, `install`, `meta` and, in `workflow`, `media`), with natural height; without `title`, only the two actions are yours.

Depends on `animated-counter`, `avatar`, `badge`, `button`, `copy-button`, `marquee`, and `segmented-control`; `HeroNav`, `HeroBackdrop`, and `HeroMark` are also exported so you can build your own version.

quandoUsar: Image galleries and feeds with varying aspect ratios (portfolios, inspiration, product photos) that load the next page when nearing the end.
Content coming from a paginated API: `loadPage(page)` receives the page number and returns the cards, and an empty list ends the feed.
quandoEvitar: Use `blog-grid` when the items are posts with text, category, and numbered pagination.
Use `pagination` with an ordinary grid when the person needs to return to an exact position or reach the page footer.
Avoid for thousands of items: there is no virtualization, and all loaded cards stay in the DOM.
acessibilidade: The container uses `role="feed"` with `aria-busy` while loading, and each card is an `article` with `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize` (−1 until the end of the feed), and the name “title by author”.
The like button exposes `aria-pressed` and a name with the total likes, and the `role="status"` footer announces loading and the end of the feed.
Fill in `alt` for each item: it is the image's alternative text; the author avatar is decorative.
movimento: New cards rise and grow slightly on a soft spring, in a cascade within the page that arrived; those that already appeared do not repeat the entrance when changing column.
While loading, each column gets a placeholder block with a shimmer passing over it and three dots bounce in the footer; liking makes the heart jump.
With “reduce motion” on, the cards only fade, the heart does not jump, the shimmer and dots stop, and the image does not zoom on hover.
responsivo: The number of columns comes from the block's own width (`minColumnWidth`, up to `maxColumns`), measured by `ResizeObserver`; columns under 200px hide the avatar.
Each image reserves its height through `ratio` before loading, so the grid does not jump when the photos arrive.
desempenho: An `IntersectionObserver` triggers `loadPage` 320px before the end and keeps requesting pages while the end is in view; images use `loading="lazy"`.
notasIA: Pass `loadPage` (without it, the block simulates four example pages) and return `[]` to end; an error also ends the feed, with no retry.
Each item needs `ratio` (image height divided by width): the block uses it to reserve space and balance the columns; repeated ids are discarded.
Likes are internal state and start empty: `onLikeChange(id, liked)` reports the change, but there is no prop to load what the person already liked.

quandoUsar: Knockout brackets for tournaments, internal championships, or prediction pools, where the person picks the winner of each match until reaching the champion.
“Who advances” simulators with 4, 8, or 16 participants, with automatic filling by the best seed and a button to start over.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` for a standings table with points and goal difference, such as round-robin or group-stage tables.
Avoid for double elimination or brackets whose number of participants is not a power of two: the block only builds single elimination and does not handle byes.
Avoid with 32 or more participants: the rounds share the width, with no horizontal scroll, and the first column gets very tall.

teclado.acao: On a team, mark it as the match winner or unmark it, if it already is; on the buttons, fill everything in (“Auto-fill”) or start over (“Reset”).

acessibilidade: Each round is a `group` with the phase name, and each team is a button with `aria-pressed` and a full name, such as “Harbor City, seed 1. Pick to win quarterfinal 1”.
The champion is announced in a `role="status"` region; the connector lines are `aria-hidden`, and the fixed texts are in English.
movimento: Choosing a winner draws its line to the next round, slides the highlight between the match's two slots, and makes the team enter the next slot coming from the left, from a slight blur.
“Auto-fill” decides one match at a time, every 0.32 s, so that each advance can be seen; the champion appears with a slightly bouncy spring.
With “reduce motion” on, lines and highlights change instantly, the teams only fade, and auto-fill does not wait between matches.
responsivo: The lines are measured from the real boxes and redrawn by `ResizeObserver` when the bracket changes size; below 44rem of container width, the names become three-letter codes and the phases get short names.
notasIA: Import `KnockoutBracket` and pass `teams` in bracket order (the first two face each other in the first match); the count must be a power of two.

Picks are `{ "rodada-partida": idDoTime }`, both counted from zero (`"0-0"` is the first match); use `value` with `onValueChange`, which already receives the picks without those that lost their meaning.
`seed` decides the “Auto-fill” (the lower number wins) and `code` appears in place of the name when the bracket gets narrow.
